test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 50% above its cost price. What percentage of discount on the marked price should be allowed to gain 8%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150.

To gain 8%, **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 8% of 100 = 108.

**Discount** = MP − SP = 150 − 108 = 42.

**Discount%** = (42 ÷ 150) × 100 = 28%.

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Markup% = 50%, Profit% = 8%.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2dd260efb35a3ce578a325b50808ae87e5a25518a8cdcd29429d4388cfa25edc.png] 
⇒ Assume **CP** = 100.
⇒ **MP** = 100 × (150 ÷ 100) = 150.
⇒ **SP** = 100 × (108 ÷ 100) = 108.
⇒ **Discount Amount** = 150 − 108 = 42.
⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (42 ÷ 150) × 100 = 28%.

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup and Discount Relation

The relation between CP and MP is given by: **CP ÷ MP = (100 − D%) ÷ (100 + P%)**.

Effective Percentage Change

Profit% can also be calculated as: **Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup × Discount) ÷ 100**.</p
